newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZKMB ups forecast export returns for NZ kiwifruit.
newsitem.headline: NZKMB ups forecast export returns for NZ kiwifruit.

text.p: Forecast export returns for New Zealand kiwifruit growers are again rising, the New Zealand Kiwifruit Marketing Board said on Friday.
Chairman John Palmer said forecasts were now up NZ$8.1 million to $265.7 million for the current selling season, the second forecast increase in two months.

He cited a record performance in the Europe market as a contributing factor to the boost. In addition, Japan and East Asia markets were showing significant volume growth and were maintaining strong prices.

Palmer said the forecast average return per tray had now moved robustly to $4.20, despite the fact that there had been a significant increase in the number of trays submitted, to 63.18 million trays this season from 58.14 million trays in 1995.
The current forecast average orchard gate return was now $16,187 per hectare compared with $14,739 in 1995.

Palmer said the higher figures were being achieved despite the significant impact of the New Zealand dollar's appreciation. He said at 1995 exchange rate levels, the forecast net market return would have been in excess of $300 million.
Among emerging markets, the best performances had been achieved in South America and Indonesia.
